subproblem.title: C¹ approximation of locally Lipschitz maps by antilipschitz C¹ pieces (Simon Ch. 2, 1.5 + inverse function theorem)
subproblem.statement: Let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on Ω. There are C¹ maps G_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q, open sets O_k ⊆ ℝⁿ and pairwise disjoint Borel sets E_k ⊆ O_k ∩ Ω (k ∈ ℕ) such that each G_k is antilipschitz on O_k (c_k|w − w′| ≤ |G_k(w) − G_k(w′)| for w, w′ ∈ O_k, some c_k > 0), u(w) = G_k(w) and u has Fréchet derivative DG_k(w) at every w ∈ E_k, and Lⁿ-almost every w ∈ Ω at which u is differentiable with injective derivative belongs to ⋃_k E_k.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n Q : ℕ) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)) (u : Eucl n → Eucl Q), IsOpen Ω → LocallyLipschitzOn Ω u → ∃ (G : ℕ → Eucl n → Eucl Q) (O E : ℕ → Set (Eucl n)), (∀ k, IsOpen (O k)) ∧ (∀ k, ContDiff ℝ 1 (G k)) ∧ (∀ k, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ O k, ∀ w' ∈ O k, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖G k w - G k w'‖) ∧ (∀ k, MeasurableSet (E k)) ∧ (∀ k, E k ⊆ O k ∩ Ω) ∧ Pairwise (Function.onFun Disjoint E) ∧ (∀ k, ∀ w ∈ E k, u w = G k w ∧ HasFDerivAt u (fderiv ℝ (G k) w) w) ∧ ∀ᵐ w ∂(volume : Measure (Eucl n)), w ∈ Ω → (∃ D : Eucl n →L[ℝ] Eucl Q, HasFDerivAt u D w ∧ Function.Injective D) → w ∈ ⋃ k, E k
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This lemma packages the C¹ Approximation Theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.5, printed proof copied in step 3) and the local inverse function theorem argument used in the parent proof (Step 5.2) and in Simon's proof of Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2. Let Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ be open and u : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on Ω. Write R := {w ∈ Ω : u is differentiable at w with injective derivative}.

1. (Case n = 0.) ℝ⁰ = {0}. If Ω = ∅ take G_k :≡ 0, O_k := ∅, E_k := ∅ for all k (all clauses hold vacuously; the antilipschitz clause with c = 1). If Ω = {0} take G_0 :≡ u(0) (constant, C¹), O_0 := ℝ⁰, E_0 := {0}, and G_k :≡ 0, O_k := ∅, E_k := ∅ for k ≥ 1. Every map on the one-point space has derivative 0 at 0 and fderiv of a constant is 0, so u(0) = G_0(0) and HasFDerivAt u (fderiv G_0 0) 0; the antilipschitz inequality is 0 ≤ … on ℝ⁰; and 0 ∈ E_0. From now on n ≥ 1 (the argument below also works for n = 0).

2. (Reduction to globally Lipschitz maps.) For each w ∈ Ω there is r > 0 with B_r(w) ⊆ Ω and u Lipschitz on B_r(w) (Ω open, u locally Lipschitz on Ω). Let B_1, B_2, … enumerate the open balls with rational centre and rational radius that are contained in Ω and on which u is Lipschitz; they cover Ω (every w lies in a rational ball inside its B_r(w)). For each m let u_m : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q be a Lipschitz extension of u|B_m (componentwise McShane extension; `LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi` composed with a linear isomorphism ℝ^Q ≅ (Fin Q → ℝ), or SimonGMT `exists_lipschitz_extension_finiteDimensional`). Then u = u_m on the open set B_m.

3. (C¹ Approximation Theorem, Simon Ch. 2, 1.5; printed proof.) Claim: if g : ℝⁿ → ℝ is Lipschitz and ε > 0, there are a closed set A ⊆ ℝⁿ with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε and h ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ) such that at every x ∈ A, g is differentiable, g(x) = h(x) and ∇g(x) = ∇h(x).
 Proof (Simon): By Rademacher's theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.4; SimonGMT `rademacher_ae_differentiableAt`) g is differentiable on a Borel set D with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ D) = 0, and ∇g is Borel measurable (Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`). By Lusin's theorem (valid for Lⁿ on ℝⁿ, a σ-finite Radon measure) there is a closed C₀ with ∇g|C₀ continuous and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C₀) < ε/4, and by inner regularity of Lⁿ there is a closed F ⊆ D with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ F) < ε/4 (Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ D) = 0); C := C₀ ∩ F is closed, C ⊆ D, ∇g|C is continuous and Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ C) < ε/2. For x, y ∈ C, x ≠ y, put R(x,y) := (g(y) − g(x) − ∇g(x)·(y − x))/|x − y|, and for k ≥ 1 put η_k(x) := sup{|R(x,y)| : y ∈ C, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k} (≤ 2 Lip g). For fixed y, x ↦ R(x,y) is continuous on C ∖ {y}, so η_k is lower semicontinuous on C, hence Borel; η_k ↓ 0 pointwise on C because g is differentiable at each x ∈ C. By Egoroff's theorem applied to the finite-measure sets C ∩ (B_j(0) ∖ B_{j−1}(0)) with tolerances ε/2^{j+3}, there is a measurable A₀ ⊆ C with Lⁿ(C ∖ A₀) < ε/4 such that η_k → 0 uniformly on each bounded subset of A₀. Choose a closed A ⊆ A₀ with Lⁿ(A₀ ∖ A) < ε/4. Then Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A) < ε, g|A and ∇g|A are continuous, and for each compact K ⊆ A: for x ∈ K, y ∈ A, 0 < |y − x| < 1/k we have |R(x,y)| ≤ η_k(x) ≤ sup_K η_k → 0, i.e. R(x,y) → 0 as y → x in A uniformly for x ∈ K. This is hypothesis (‡) of the Whitney Extension Theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.6; see [EG92, §6.5], [Fed69, 3.1.14]; partial Lean machinery: SimonGMT `HasWhitneyC1Compatibility.hasFDerivAt_whitneyExtension` in Chapter02/WhitneyExtension.lean), which yields h ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ) with h = g and ∇h = ∇g on A. At x ∈ A ⊆ D, g is differentiable. □
 Apply the claim to each component u_m^l (l = 1,…,Q) with ε := 1/(i·max(Q,1)) and intersect the Q closed sets (if Q = 0 take A_{m,i} := ℝⁿ and G_{m,i} :≡ 0; every map into ℝ⁰ is differentiable with derivative 0): for every m and i ≥ 1 there are a closed A_{m,i} with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ ∖ A_{m,i}) < 1/i and G_{m,i} ∈ C¹(ℝⁿ;ℝ^Q) such that at every w ∈ A_{m,i}: u_m is differentiable (all components are), u_m(w) = G_{m,i}(w) and Du_m(w) = DG_{m,i}(w).

4. (Covering of R.) Let w ∈ R ∩ B_m. As u = u_m on the open set B_m, u_m is differentiable at w with Du_m(w) = Du(w), which is injective. So R ∩ B_m ∖ ⋃_i A_{m,i} ⊆ ⋂_i (ℝⁿ ∖ A_{m,i}), which has measure ≤ 1/i for every i, hence is Lⁿ-null. Put D_{m,i} := {w ∈ B_m ∩ A_{m,i} : DG_{m,i}(w) is injective}. For w ∈ R ∩ B_m ∩ A_{m,i} we have DG_{m,i}(w) = Du_m(w) = Du(w) injective, so w ∈ D_{m,i}. Since R ⊆ ⋃_m B_m, we get Lⁿ(R ∖ ⋃_{m,i} D_{m,i}) = 0. Each D_{m,i} is Borel: B_m is open, A_{m,i} is closed, and {w : DG_{m,i}(w) injective} is open (DG_{m,i} is continuous and injectivity of a linear map ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q is an open condition, being equivalent to min_{|s|=1}|As| > 0).

5. (Local antilipschitz property — inverse function theorem argument.) Let w ∈ D_{m,i}, G := G_{m,i}, A := DG(w) and c := ½ min_{|s|=1} |As| > 0. By continuity of DG there is r > 0 with ‖DG(z) − DG(w)‖ ≤ c for |z − w| < r. For z, z′ ∈ B_r(w) (a convex set), the mean value inequality applied to z ↦ G(z) − Az gives |G(z) − G(z′) − A(z − z′)| ≤ c|z − z′|, hence |G(z) − G(z′)| ≥ |A(z − z′)| − c|z − z′| ≥ 2c|z − z′| − c|z − z′| = c|z − z′|. So G is c-antilipschitz on B_r(w), hence on every rational ball O with w ∈ O ⊆ B_r(w) ∩ B_m (such O exists). Let 𝒪_{m,i} be the countable set of rational open balls O ⊆ B_m on which G_{m,i} is c-antilipschitz for some c > 0; then D_{m,i} ⊆ ⋃_{O ∈ 𝒪_{m,i}} O.

6. (The pieces.) Enumerate the countable set of triples (m, i, O) with O ∈ 𝒪_{m,i} as k = 0, 1, 2, … (pad with G_k :≡ 0, O_k := ∅, E′_k := ∅ if it is finite), and set G_k := G_{m,i}, O_k := O, E′_k := D_{m,i} ∩ O, and finally E_k := E′_k ∖ ⋃_{l<k} E′_l. Verification:
 • O_k is open; G_k is C¹ (`ContDiff ℝ 1`); G_k is antilipschitz on O_k with some c > 0 (definition of 𝒪_{m,i}).
 • E_k is Borel (step 4), E_k ⊆ O ⊆ B_m ⊆ Ω, so E_k ⊆ O_k ∩ Ω; the E_k are pairwise disjoint by construction.
 • For w ∈ E_k ⊆ B_m ∩ A_{m,i}: u(w) = u_m(w) = G_k(w); and since u = u_m on the open set B_m ∋ w and u_m is differentiable at w with Du_m(w) = DG_k(w) = fderiv ℝ G_k w, we get HasFDerivAt u (fderiv ℝ G_k w) w.
 • ⋃_k E_k = ⋃_k E′_k = ⋃_{m,i} D_{m,i} (each w ∈ D_{m,i} lies in some O ∈ 𝒪_{m,i}). By step 4, Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω at which u is differentiable with injective derivative (i.e. w ∈ R) lies in ⋃_k E_k. This is the last clause, stated with `volume` = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cover Ω by countably many rational balls B_m on which u is Lipschitz and extend u|B_m to Lipschitz u_m on ℝⁿ.

C¹ Approximation Theorem (Simon Ch. 2, 1.5: Rademacher + Lusin + Egoroff + Whitney extension), componentwise: closed A_{m,i} with Lⁿ(ℝⁿ∖A_{m,i}) < 1/i on which u_m is differentiable, u_m = G_{m,i} and Du_m = DG_{m,i}.
Lⁿ-a.e. point where u is differentiable with injective derivative lies in a Borel set D_{m,i} where DG_{m,i} is injective.
Mean value inequality: G_{m,i} is antilipschitz on a small ball around each point of D_{m,i}; use countably many rational balls O.
Enumerate the triples (m,i,O), take E_k := D_{m,i} ∩ O and disjointify; u = G_k with Du = DG_k on E_k.

subproblem.title: Simple n-vectors: Gram-determinant norm and change of frame (parent P1)
subproblem.statement: For all P, n and every family v = (v₁,…,v_n) in ℝ^P, the operator norm of the simple n-vector simpleNVector v (the functional α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n) on n-covectors, which carry the multilinear operator norm) satisfies ‖simpleNVector v‖² = det(⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j}; and for every real n×n matrix B and every τ = (τ₁,…,τ_n) in ℝ^P, simpleNVector(i ↦ Σ_j B_ij τ_j) = det(B)·simpleNVector τ.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → Eucl P), ‖simpleNVector v‖ ^ 2 = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)).det) ∧ ∀ (P n : ℕ) (B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) (τ : Fin n → Eucl P), simpleNVector (fun i => ∑ j, B i j • τ j) = B.det • simpleNVector τ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

Throughout, G(v) := (⟨v_i, v_j⟩)_{i,j} is the Gram matrix of v = (v₁,…,v_n) and, for a real n×n matrix B and τ = (τ₁,…,τ_n), (Bτ)_i := Σ_j B_ij τ_j. This is item (P1) of the parent proof.

1. (Second identity: change of frame.) Let α be any n-covector. By multilinearity,
 α(Bτ) = Σ_{g : Fin n → Fin n} (Π_i B_{i g(i)}) · α(τ_{g(1)}, …, τ_{g(n)}).
 If g is not injective two arguments coincide and the term vanishes because α is alternating. If g = σ is a permutation, α(τ∘σ) = sign(σ) α(τ). Hence α(Bτ) = (Σ_σ sign(σ) Π_i B_{iσ(i)}) α(τ) = det(B) α(τ) by the Leibniz formula (det B = det Bᵀ, so the row/column convention is immaterial). As this holds for every α, simpleNVector(Bτ) = det(B) • simpleNVector τ. For n = 0 both sides are the functional α ↦ α(∅) and the determinant of the empty matrix is 1.

2. (Gram matrices transform by congruence.) G(Bτ)_{ik} = ⟨Σ_j B_ij τ_j, Σ_l B_kl τ_l⟩ = (B G(τ) Bᵀ)_{ik}; hence det G(Bτ) = det(B)² det G(τ).

3. (Upper bound for orthonormal families.) If τ is orthonormal then |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|τ_i| = ‖α‖ for every α, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ 1.

4. (Lower bound for orthonormal families.) Let τ be orthonormal (n ≥ 1), W := span τ and π_W the orthogonal projection onto W. Define α₀(u₁,…,u_n) := det(⟨u_i, τ_j⟩)_{i,j}. It is n-linear and alternating (a determinant whose i-th row depends linearly on u_i, and two equal u's give two equal rows) and continuous (finite dimension). The i-th row (⟨u_i,τ_j⟩)_j is the coordinate vector of π_W u_i in the orthonormal basis τ, of Euclidean length |π_W u_i| ≤ |u_i|. By Hadamard's inequality |det A| ≤ Π_i |row_i(A)| (proof: if the rows are dependent det A = 0; otherwise Gram–Schmidt on the rows gives A = R O with O orthogonal and R lower triangular with diagonal entries |a_i^⊥| ≤ |a_i|, a_i^⊥ the component of the i-th row orthogonal to the previous rows, so |det A| = Π|a_i^⊥| ≤ Π|a_i|; in Lean this is `Orientation.abs_volumeForm_apply_le` for the volume form of W composed with π_W) we get |α₀(u)| ≤ Π|u_i|, i.e. ‖α₀‖ ≤ 1. Since α₀(τ) = det(⟨τ_i,τ_j⟩) = det I = 1, ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≥ |simpleNVector τ (α₀)| / ‖α₀‖ ≥ 1. Together with step 3: ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1 = det G(τ). For n = 0, 0-covectors are the constants c = α(∅) with ‖α‖ = |c|, so ‖simpleNVector ∅‖ = 1 = det of the empty matrix.

5. (Dependent families.) If v₁,…,v_n are linearly dependent then α(v) = 0 for every alternating α (`AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent`), so simpleNVector v = 0 and ‖simpleNVector v‖² = 0. Also G(v) is singular: for a nontrivial c with Σ_j c_j v_j = 0 we get G(v)c = (⟨v_i, Σ_j c_j v_j⟩)_i = 0, so det G(v) = 0. The first identity holds. (This covers in particular n > P.)

6. (Independent families.) If v is linearly independent, Gram–Schmidt produces an orthonormal τ with span τ = span v and v = Bτ, B_ij = ⟨v_i, τ_j⟩, B invertible. By step 1, simpleNVector v = det(B) • simpleNVector τ, so by step 4, ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |det B|. By step 2 and G(τ) = I, det G(v) = det(B)². Hence ‖simpleNVector v‖² = det G(v) = det (Matrix.of fun i j => ⟨v_i, v_j⟩).

Steps 5–6 give the first conjunct for every v; step 1 gives the second conjunct. ∎
proof_key_steps: Leibniz expansion and the alternating property give α(Bτ) = det(B)·α(τ) for every n-covector α, hence simpleNVector(Bτ) = det(B)•simpleNVector τ.
Gram matrices transform by congruence: det G(Bτ) = det(B)²·det G(τ).
For orthonormal τ: ‖simpleNVector τ‖ ≤ Π|τ_i| = 1, and the covector det(⟨u_i,τ_j⟩) has norm ≤ 1 by Hadamard and value 1 at τ, so ‖simpleNVector τ‖ = 1.
Dependent families: simpleNVector v = 0 and det G(v) = 0.
Independent families: Gram–Schmidt v = Bτ gives ‖simpleNVector v‖ = |det B| and det G(v) = det(B)².

Recall η_{y,λ}(z) := λ⁻¹(z − y) (`blowUpMap y λ`) and that HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y P means: dim P = n and for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q), ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y + λz) dHⁿ(z) → θ(y) ∫_P φ dHⁿ as λ ↓ 0. If n > Q then Hⁿ ≡ 0 on ℝ^Q (Hausdorff dimension of ℝ^Q is Q; `hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt`) and there is nothing to prove; assume n ≤ Q.

0. (Preliminaries on the chart.)
 (a) For w ∈ Ω and s ∈ ℝⁿ: w + ts ∈ Ω for small t, and |Φ(w+ts) − Φ(w)| ≥ c|t||s|; dividing by |t| and letting t → 0 gives |DΦ(w)s| ≥ c|s|. So DΦ(w) is injective and T_w := DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w) has dimension n. Φ is injective on Ω; for y ∈ N let w_y ∈ Ω be the unique point with Φ(w_y) = y, and T_y := T_{w_y}. (The Lean conclusion “∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → …” concerns exactly w = w_y.)
 (b) Ψ := (Φ|Ω)⁻¹ : N → Ω is (1/c)-Lipschitz. N is σ-compact (Ω is a countable union of compact sets and Φ is continuous), hence Borel; M ∩ N is Hⁿ-null-measurable.
 (c) N is locally Hⁿ-finite: if K ⊆ ℝ^Q is compact, Ψ(N ∩ K) has diameter ≤ diam(K)/c, so lies in a closed ball B̄ ⊆ ℝⁿ; Φ is Lipschitz on B̄ (C¹ on a compact convex set), say with constant Λ, and Hⁿ(N ∩ K) ≤ Λⁿ Lⁿ(B̄) < ∞.
 (d) (Change of variables under blow-ups.) η_{y,λ} is a similarity of ratio λ⁻¹, so for every set S and every g ≥ 0 or Hⁿ⌞S-integrable g: ∫_{η_{y,λ}(S)} g dHⁿ = λ^{−n} ∫_S g∘η_{y,λ} dHⁿ (translation invariance and μHE[n](λS) = λⁿ μHE[n](S), Mathlib `euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀`).
 (e) (C¹ blow-up of N; Simon: “since x ∈ N_j and N_j is a C¹ submanifold, lim ∫_{η(N_j)} f = ∫_{T N_j} f”.) For every y ∈ N and φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q): lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ. Proof: let spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), w := w_y. By (d) and the injective area formula for Φ on Ω (Φ injective, Lipschitz on bounded subsets of Ω; Simon Ch. 2 (3.2)/(3.5), SimonGMT `injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn` and its weighted fibre-sum form) the integral equals λ^{−n} ∫_Ω φ((Φ(v) − y)/λ) JΦ(v) dv, JΦ(v) := √det(DΦ(v)*DΦ(v)), and the substitution v = w + λs turns it into I_λ := ∫ 1_{(Ω−w)/λ}(s) φ((Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w))/λ) JΦ(w+λs) ds. If the integrand is nonzero then w, w + λs ∈ Ω and |Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w)| < λR, so c|λs| < λR, i.e. |s| < R/c. For λ ≤ 1 the integrand is bounded by sup|φ| · max_{|z−w| ≤ R/c} JΦ(z) and vanishes for |s| ≥ R/c; for fixed s, as λ ↓ 0: w + λs ∈ Ω eventually (Ω open), (Φ(w+λs) − Φ(w))/λ → DΦ(w)s and JΦ(w+λs) → JΦ(w). By dominated convergence I_λ → ∫_{ℝⁿ} φ(DΦ(w)s) JΦ(w) ds = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ, the last equality being the linear area formula for the injective linear map DΦ(w) (Simon Ch. 2 (3.1); Mathlib `LinearMap.hausdorffMeasure_image`/normDet). Note that for nonnegative φ ≥ 1_{B_R(0)} this also shows sup_{0<λ≤1} λ^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{λR}(y)) < ∞.
 (f) (Upper Density Theorem, Simon Ch. 1, 3.6; SimonGMT `Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6`.) If μ is a Borel regular measure on ℝ^Q and A is μ-measurable with μ(A) < ∞, then for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ ℝ^Q ∖ A, lim_{ρ↓0} ρ^{−n} μ(A ∩ B_ρ(y)) = 0. (Finite Borel measures on ℝ^Q, and Hⁿ restricted to sets of finite measure, are Borel regular.)

1. (Compact pieces with continuous weight — Remark 1.8(1).) Let V_1 ⊆ V_2 ⊆ ⋯ be open sets with compact closures closure V_i ⊆ V_{i+1} ⊆ V and ⋃_i V_i = V. Fix i. ν_i(B) := ∫_{B ∩ M ∩ V_i} θ dHⁿ defines a finite Borel measure (∫_{M ∩ closure V_i} θ < ∞), and θ is ν_i-measurable (θ is a.e. strongly measurable on M ∩ closure V_i by `IntegrableOn`). Choose a Borel M_i′ ⊆ M ∩ V_i with Hⁿ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ M_i′) = 0. For each j ≥ 1, Lusin's theorem for the finite Borel measure ν_i (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT `Chapter01.Lusin`) gives a closed F with ν_i(ℝ^Q ∖ F) < 1/(2j) and θ|F continuous, and inner regularity gives a compact C_{i,j} ⊆ M_i′ ∩ F with ν_i((M_i′ ∩ F) ∖ C_{i,j}) < 1/(2j). Thus C_{i,j} ⊆ M ∩ V_i is compact, θ|C_{i,j} is continuous and ν_i((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C_{i,j}) < 1/j. Hence ν_i((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) = 0, and since θ > 0 on M, also Hⁿ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) = 0. As M = ⋃_i (M ∩ V_i), it suffices to prove: for each fixed C := C_{i,j}, the conclusion holds at Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N. Note that θ ≥ m_C := min_C θ > 0 on C (continuous positive function on a compact set), so Hⁿ(C) ≤ m_C^{−1} ∫_C θ dHⁿ < ∞.

2. (Unweighted tangent plane of C on the chart — proof of 1.6 “⇒”.) Exceptional sets, by (f):
 (i) μ := Hⁿ⌞C (finite), A := C ∖ N: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0.
 (ii) For each of the countably many rational balls B ⊆ ℝ^Q, μ := Hⁿ⌞(N ∩ B) (finite by (c)), A := (N ∩ B) ∖ C: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ B, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0; since B_ρ(y) ⊆ B for small ρ when y ∈ B, and the rational balls cover ℝ^Q: for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C ∩ N, ρ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B_ρ(y)) → 0.
 Let y ∈ C ∩ N satisfy (i) and (ii). For φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) with spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), using (d),
 ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ = ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N)} φ − ∫_{η_{y,λ}(N ∖ C)} φ + ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C ∖ N)} φ,
 and |∫_{η_{y,λ}(N∖C)} φ| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} Hⁿ((N ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, |∫_{η_{y,λ}(C∖N)} φ| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, while the first term tends to ∫_{T_y} φ by (e). Hence lim_{λ↓0} ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ dHⁿ = ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ for every φ (the exceptional set does not depend on φ). Moreover λ^{−n} Hⁿ(C ∩ B_{λR}(y)) ≤ λ^{−n} Hⁿ(N ∩ B_{λR}(y)) + λ^{−n} Hⁿ((C ∖ N) ∩ B_{λR}(y)) stays bounded as λ ↓ 0 (by (e) and (i)).

3. (Exceptional set for the rest of M.) By (f) with μ := ν_i and A := (M ∩ V_i) ∖ C (ν_i(A) < ∞): for Hⁿ-a.e. y ∈ C, ρ^{−n} ∫_{((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C) ∩ B_ρ(y)} θ dHⁿ → 0.

4. (Weighted blow-up — Remark 1.8(1).) Let y ∈ C ∩ N satisfy the conclusions of steps 2 and 3, let φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q) with spt φ ⊆ B_R(0), and let λ > 0 be so small that closure B_{λR}(y) ⊆ V_i (possible: y ∈ C ⊆ V_i open). Then z ↦ φ(z)θ(y + λz) is Hⁿ-integrable on η_{y,λ}(M): it vanishes unless y + λz ∈ M ∩ B_{λR}(y), and by (d) its absolute integral is ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} ∫_{M ∩ closure B_{λR}(y)} θ < ∞. By (d),
 ∫_{η_{y,λ}(M)} φ(z) θ(y+λz) dHⁿ(z) = λ^{−n} ∫_M φ((x−y)/λ) θ(x) dHⁿ(x) = I₁ + I₂ + I₃, where
 I₁ := θ(y) λ^{−n} ∫_C φ((x−y)/λ) dHⁿ(x) = θ(y) ∫_{η_{y,λ}(C)} φ dHⁿ → θ(y) ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ (step 2);
 I₂ := λ^{−n} ∫_{C ∩ B_{λR}(y)} φ((x−y)/λ)(θ(x) − θ(y)) dHⁿ(x), |I₂| ≤ sup|φ| · sup_{C ∩ B_{λR}(y)} |θ − θ(y)| · λ^{−n} Hⁿ(C ∩ B_{λR}(y)) → 0, because θ|C is continuous at y and the density ratio is bounded (step 2);
 I₃ := λ^{−n} ∫_{(M ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)} φ((x−y)/λ) θ(x) dHⁿ(x), and since (M ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y) = ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ C) ∩ B_{λR}(y), |I₃| ≤ sup|φ| λ^{−n} ∫_{((M∩V_i)∖C) ∩ B_{λR}(y)} θ dHⁿ → 0 (step 3).
 Hence the weighted blow-up integrals converge to θ(y) ∫_{T_y} φ dHⁿ for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^Q); together with dim T_y = n (0(a)) this is HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y T_y with T_y = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w_y).

5. (Conclusion.) The set of y ∈ M ∩ N where the conclusion fails is contained in ⋃_i ((M ∩ V_i) ∖ ⋃_j C_{i,j}) ∪ ⋃_{i,j} (the exceptional subsets of C_{i,j} ∩ N from steps 2–3), a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets. Since M ∩ N is Hⁿ-null-measurable (0(b)), this is exactly the statement “∀ᵐ y ∂ Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ Φ(Ω)), ∀ w ∈ Ω, Φ w = y → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (range DΦ(w))”. ∎
 (For n = 0 all steps hold verbatim: ℝ⁰ is a point, H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] is counting measure, λ⁰ = 1, N is a single point or empty and T_y = {0}.)
proof_key_steps: Chart facts: DΦ(w) injective with |DΦ(w)s| ≥ c|s|, Φ(Ω) σ-compact and locally Hⁿ-finite, inverse (1/c)-Lipschitz.
C¹ blow-up: via the injective area formula and dominated convergence, blow-ups of Φ(Ω) at y = Φ(w) converge to Hⁿ⌞DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ).
Remark 1.8(1): by Lusin, M ∩ V_i is covered up to null sets by compact C with θ|C continuous and Hⁿ(C) < ∞.
Proof of 1.6 ⇒: by the Upper Density Theorem, Hⁿ⌞(C∖N) and Hⁿ⌞(N∖C) have zero density at a.e. point of C ∩ N, so blow-ups of C converge to T_y with bounded density ratios.
Weighted blow-up of (M,θ) = θ(y)·blow-up of C + continuity error on C + θHⁿ⌞(M∖C) term of zero density, giving the weighted tangent space T_y.

subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, f locally Lipschitz on U, and L : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) such that for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, t ↦ f(x + tv) has derivative L(x)v at 0 for every v in every weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x. Let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be C¹ and antilipschitz on an open Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M): DΦ(w)(ℝⁿ) is the weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at Φ(w), and f∘Φ has Fréchet derivative L(Φ(w))∘DΦ(w) at w.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q) (L : Eucl P → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q)) (Φ : Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : Set (Eucl n)), IsOpen U → IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∀ Tx : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Tx → ∀ v ∈ Tx, HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => f (x + t • v)) (L x v) 0) → IsOpen Ω → ContDiff ℝ 1 Φ → (∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω, ∀ w' ∈ Ω, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ w - Φ w'‖) → ∀ᵐ w ∂((volume : Measure (Eucl n)).restrict (Ω ∩ Φ ⁻¹' M)), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (Φ w) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ Φ w).toLinearMap) ∧ HasFDerivAt (f ∘ Φ) ((L (Φ w)).comp (fderiv ℝ Φ w)) w
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is the chain-rule part of Step 2 and Step 5.2 of the parent proof (“the chain rule applied to u = (f∘Φ_x)∘(Φ_x⁻¹∘Φ) gives Du(w) = d^Mf_x∘DΦ(w)”), formulated for an arbitrary admissible L. Setting: U ⊆ ℝ^P open, IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, f locally Lipschitz on U, L satisfying the derivative clause for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P of class C¹ and c-antilipschitz on the open set Ω. We use:
(DD) (Simon Ch. 2, 4.7–4.10.) Let f be K-Lipschitz on a ball B_ρ(x) ⊆ ℝ^P, let Φ be differentiable at w with Φ(w) = x and f∘Φ differentiable at w. Then for every s ∈ ℝⁿ, t ↦ f(x + t·DΦ(w)s) is differentiable at t = 0 with derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s. Proof: for small |t| both x + t·DΦ(w)s and Φ(w+ts) lie in B_ρ(x), so |f(x + t·DΦ(w)s) − f(Φ(w+ts))| ≤ K|Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s − Φ(w+ts)| = o(t), and f(Φ(w+ts)) = f(x) + t·D(f∘Φ)(w)s + o(t).

1. (Null sets transfer to the parameter domain.) Ψ := (Φ|Ω)⁻¹ : Φ(Ω) → Ω is (1/c)-Lipschitz, so for every Z ⊆ Φ(Ω) with Hⁿ(Z) = 0 we get Lⁿ(Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z)) = Hⁿ(Ψ(Z)) ≤ c^{−n} Hⁿ(Z) = 0 (Lipschitz image bound; on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = μHE[n] = Lⁿ = volume). Also Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) is Lⁿ-null-measurable: writing M = B ∪ Z₀ with B Borel and Hⁿ(Z₀) = 0, Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(B) is Borel and Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(Z₀) is Lⁿ-null; so “Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M)” is the a.e. filter of volume.restrict (Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M)).

2. (Tangent identification.) By the sibling lemma weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart with (Q, V, M, θ, Φ, Ω) := (P, U, M, θ, Φ, Ω) (hypotheses: fields `subset`, `nullMeasurableSet`, `pos`, `integrableOn` of the triple; Φ C¹ and antilipschitz on Ω), the set Z₁ of y ∈ M ∩ Φ(Ω) at which HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y (range DΦ(Ψ y)) fails is Hⁿ-null. By step 1, for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M): HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (Φ w) (range DΦ(w)). This is the first conjunct.

3. (Derivative clause transfers.) The set Z₂ of x ∈ M at which the derivative clause for L fails is Hⁿ-null (the hypothesis is an a.e. statement for Hⁿ⌞M and M is null-measurable). By step 1, for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) the clause holds at x := Φ(w).

4. (Rademacher.) u := f∘Φ is locally Lipschitz on the open set Ω′ := Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U) ⊇ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(M) (Φ is C¹, hence Lipschitz near each point, and f is locally Lipschitz on the open set U). subproblem.title: C¹ chart cover of countably n-rectifiable sets (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2)
subproblem.statement: If M ⊆ ℝ^P is countably n-rectifiable, there are C¹ maps Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and open sets Ω_j ⊆ ℝⁿ (j ∈ ℕ) such that each Φ_j is Lipschitz and antilipschitz on Ω_j and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Eucl P)), CountablyRectifiable n M → ∃ (Φ : ℕ → Eucl n → Eucl P) (Ω : ℕ → Set (Eucl n)), (∀ j, IsOpen (Ω j)) ∧ (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ 1 (Φ j)) ∧ (∀ j, ∃ K : ℝ≥0, LipschitzOnWith K (Φ j) (Ω j)) ∧ (∀ j, ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ w ∈ Ω j, ∀ w' ∈ Ω j, c * ‖w - w'‖ ≤ ‖Φ j w - Φ j w'‖) ∧ (μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)) (M \ ⋃ j, Φ j '' Ω j) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2, “only if” part (printed proof adapted), used in Step 1 of the parent proof (Remark 1.3). Let M be countably n-rectifiable: M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_{j≥1} F_j(ℝⁿ) with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P Lipschitz (Definition 1.1).

1. Fix j. Apply the sibling lemma lipschitz_c1_immersion_pieces to u := F_j and Ω := ℝⁿ (open; F_j is Lipschitz, hence locally Lipschitz): we get C¹ maps G_{j,k} : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, open O_{j,k} with G_{j,k} antilipschitz on O_{j,k}, and Borel E_{j,k} ⊆ O_{j,k} with F_j = G_{j,k} on E_{j,k}, such that Lⁿ-a.e. w at which F_j is differentiable with injective derivative lies in ⋃_k E_{j,k}.

2. Decompose ℝⁿ = N_j ∪ C_j ∪ R_j, where N_j := {w : F_j not differentiable at w}, C_j := {w : F_j differentiable at w, DF_j(w) not injective}, R_j := {w : F_j differentiable at w, DF_j(w) injective}. These sets are Borel (the differentiability set is Borel and w ↦ fderiv F_j w is Borel measurable, Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`). By Rademacher's theorem Lⁿ(N_j) = 0, and by step 1 Lⁿ(R_j ∖ ⋃_k E_{j,k}) = 0.

3. Hⁿ(F_j(N_j ∪ (R_j ∖ ⋃_k E_{j,k}))) = 0: F_j is Lipschitz with constant Λ_j, so Hⁿ(F_j(Z)) ≤ Λ_jⁿ Hⁿ(Z) = Λ_jⁿ Lⁿ(Z) = 0 for every Lⁿ-null Z ⊆ ℝⁿ (on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ = μHE[n] = Lⁿ).

4. Hⁿ(F_j(C_j)) = 0, by the area formula (Simon: “by the area formula Lⁿ{x : JG_ij = 0} …”). In Lean this is directly SimonGMT `area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero` (Chapter02/AreaLipschitz.lean: critical and non-differentiability images of a Lipschitz map are Hⁿ-null). Mathematically: for the Lipschitz map F_j on the Borel set C_j, Simon Ch. 2 (3.4) (SimonGMT `area_formula_lipschitzOn_multiplicity`) gives ∫_{ℝ^P} #(C_j ∩ F_j⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{C_j} JF_j dLⁿ, where JF_j(w) = √det(DF_j(w)* DF_j(w)) (Jacobian of the within derivative, which agrees a.e. on C_j with DF_j). For w ∈ C_j, DF_j(w)*DF_j(w) is singular, so JF_j = 0 a.e. on C_j and the right side is 0. F_j(C_j) is Hⁿ-null-measurable (C_j is a countable union of bounded Borel sets of finite measure and F_j is Lipschitz; SimonGMT `nullMeasurableSet_image_of_lipschitzOn`), and the multiplicity is ≥ 1 on F_j(C_j), so Hⁿ(F_j(C_j)) = ∫ 1_{F_j(C_j)} dHⁿ ≤ ∫ #(C_j ∩ F_j⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = 0.

5. For w ∈ E_{j,k}, F_j(w) = G_{j,k}(w) ∈ G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}). Hence F_j(ℝⁿ) ⊆ F_j(N_j ∪ (R_j ∖ ⋃_k E_{j,k})) ∪ F_j(C_j) ∪ ⋃_k G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}).

6. (Lipschitz bound by shrinking.) Each open O_{j,k} is the union of the countably many open balls B with rational centre and rational radius and closure B ⊆ O_{j,k}. On such B, ‖DG_{j,k}‖ is bounded on the compact convex set closure B, so by the mean value inequality G_{j,k} is Lipschitz on B (constant sup_{closure B}‖DG_{j,k}‖); and G_{j,k} is antilipschitz on B ⊆ O_{j,k} with the constant of O_{j,k}. Enumerate all triples (j, k, B) as l = 0, 1, 2, … (pad with Ω_l := ∅ if needed) and set Φ_l := G_{j,k}, Ω_l := B. Then each Ω_l is open, Φ_l is C¹ (`ContDiff ℝ 1`), Lipschitz and antilipschitz on Ω_l, and ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l) = ⋃_{j,k} G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}).

7. By steps 3–6, M ∖ ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l) ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j [F_j(N_j ∪ (R_j ∖ ⋃_k E_{j,k})) ∪ F_j(C_j)], a countable union of Hⁿ-null sets. Hence Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_l Φ_l(Ω_l)) = 0. ∎ (When n > P every set in ℝ^P is Hⁿ-null and the statement is immediate; the proof above also covers it.)

Images of the non-differentiability set and of the uncovered regular set are Hⁿ-null (Rademacher, Lipschitz image bound).
The image of the critical set is Hⁿ-null by the area formula (Jacobian 0 there).
On E_{j,k}, F_j = G_{j,k}, so F_j(ℝⁿ) is covered up to null sets by the antilipschitz C¹ pieces G_{j,k}(O_{j,k}).
Shrink each O_{j,k} to rational balls with compact closure inside to make the charts Lipschitz too; enumerate.

ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is item (P2) of the parent proof. Recall spt T = T.support = U ∖ Z_T, where Z_T (the zero region) is the union of all open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U, on which T vanishes (T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ Dⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W).

1. Since M ⊆ U (field `subset`), M ∖ spt T ⊆ Z_T.

2. Z_T is an open subset of the second countable space ℝ^P, hence Lindelöf; so there are countably many sets W_k of the defining family with Z_T = ⋃_k W_k. By countable subadditivity it suffices to prove Hⁿ(M ∩ W) = 0 for every open W with K := closure W compact, K ⊆ U, on which T vanishes.

3. (ξ has unit norm a.e.) By the field `orients`, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with ξ(x) = simpleNVector τ or ξ(x) = −simpleNVector τ. By the sibling lemma simple_nvector_algebra (first conjunct, with G(τ) = I), ‖simpleNVector τ‖² = det I = 1. Hence ‖ξ(x)‖ = 1 for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M; in particular ξ(x) ≠ 0 and |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖ for every n-covector α. (If no orthonormal n-family exists, e.g. n > P, this a.e. statement already forces Hⁿ(M) = 0 and the lemma holds; the argument below covers this case too.)

subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on U. There is L : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) such that (a) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, for every subspace T_x that is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x and every v ∈ T_x, t ↦ f(x + tv) is differentiable at t = 0 with derivative L(x)v; (b) L is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable; (c) for every compact K ⊆ U, sup_{x ∈ M ∩ K} ‖L(x)‖ < ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), IsOpen U → IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → ∃ L : Eucl P → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q), (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∀ Tx : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Tx → ∀ v ∈ Tx, HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => f (x + t • v)) (L x v) 0) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable L ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) ∧ ∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ M ∩ K, ‖L x‖ ≤ C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is Steps 1–2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 3 §2, 2.1–2.2 and p. 76), with the C¹ decomposition supplied by the siblings. Setting: U ⊆ ℝ^P open, IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, f locally Lipschitz on U. We use the elementary fact
(DD) (Directional derivatives along a chart; Simon Ch. 2, 4.7–4.10, and Step 2 of the parent proof.) Let f be K-Lipschitz on a ball B_ρ(x) ⊆ ℝ^P, let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be differentiable at w with Φ(w) = x, and let f∘Φ be differentiable at w. Then for every s ∈ ℝⁿ the map t ↦ f(x + t·DΦ(w)s) is differentiable at t = 0 with derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s, and |D(f∘Φ)(w)s| ≤ K|DΦ(w)s|. Proof: as t → 0, both x + t·DΦ(w)s and Φ(w + ts) tend to x, so they lie in B_ρ(x) for small |t|; then |f(x + t·DΦ(w)s) − f(Φ(w+ts))| ≤ K|Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s − Φ(w+ts)| = o(t) by differentiability of Φ at w, and f(Φ(w+ts)) = f(x) + t·D(f∘Φ)(w)s + o(t) by differentiability of f∘Φ at w. Hence f(x + t·DΦ(w)s) = f(x) + t·D(f∘Φ)(w)s + o(t). Finally |f(x + t·DΦ(w)s) − f(x)| ≤ K|t||DΦ(w)s| for small t, so the derivative has norm ≤ K|DΦ(w)s|.

1. (Charts.) By the sibling lemma countably_rectifiable_c1_cover applied to the countably n-rectifiable set M (field `countablyRectifiable`) there are C¹ maps Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and open Ω_j ⊆ ℝⁿ such that Φ_j is K_j-Lipschitz and c_j-antilipschitz on Ω_j and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0. Replace Ω_j by the open set Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(U); all properties persist and, as M ⊆ U, the covering property is unchanged. Each Φ_j(Ω_j) is σ-compact, hence Borel, and Ψ_j := (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹ : Φ_j(Ω_j) → Ω_j is (1/c_j)-Lipschitz, in particular continuous. Put P_j := Φ_j(Ω_j) ∖ ⋃_{i<j} Φ_i(Ω_i) (Borel, pairwise disjoint, ⋃_j P_j = ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)), and u_j := f∘Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q.

2. (Definition of L.) For x ∈ P_j let w := Ψ_j(x), A := DΦ_j(w) (injective, since |As| ≥ c_j|s| by the antilipschitz property on the open set Ω_j) and A⁺ := (A*A)⁻¹A* : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ (so A⁺A = id_{ℝⁿ}, AA⁺ = π_x, the orthogonal projection onto range A, and A⁺ = A⁺π_x); define L(x) := fderiv ℝ u_j w ∘ A⁺ (Mathlib's fderiv, which is 0 where u_j is not differentiable). For x ∉ ⋃_j P_j define L(x) := 0.

3. (Measurability.) On P_j, x ↦ L(x) is the composition of the continuous map Ψ_j, the Borel map w ↦ fderiv ℝ u_j w (Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`), the continuous map w ↦ DΦ_j(w), and the continuous map A ↦ A⁺ on the open set of injective linear maps; composition of linear maps is continuous. Hence L is Borel measurable on ℝ^P (countably many Borel pieces, 0 elsewhere), and since its values lie in the finite-dimensional space L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q), L is strongly measurable, in particular AEStronglyMeasurable for Hⁿ⌞M.

4. (Good set.) The following sets are Hⁿ-null: (a) M ∖ ⋃_j P_j (step 1); (b) for each j, Φ_j(Z_j), where Z_j ⊆ Ω_j is the set where u_j is not differentiable: u_j is locally Lipschitz on the open set Ω_j (f locally Lipschitz on U ⊇ Φ_j(Ω_j), Φ_j Lipschitz), so by Rademacher's theorem (applied to Lipschitz extensions of u_j on countably many balls covering Ω_j; SimonGMT `rademacher_ae_differentiableAt`) Lⁿ(Z_j) = 0, and Hⁿ(Φ_j(Z_j)) ≤ K_jⁿ Lⁿ(Z_j) = 0; (c) for each j, the set of x ∈ M ∩ Φ_j(Ω_j) at which HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x (range DΦ_j(Ψ_j x)) fails: by the sibling lemma weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart, applied with (Q, V, M, θ, Φ, Ω) := (P, U, M, θ, Φ_j, Ω_j), whose hypotheses are the fields `subset`, `nullMeasurableSet`, `pos`, `integrableOn` of the triple. Let G be M minus the union of these null sets; Hⁿ(M ∖ G) = 0.

5. (The derivative clause.) Let x ∈ G, so x ∈ P_j for some j; put w := Ψ_j(x), A := DΦ_j(w), B := Du_j(w) (u_j is differentiable at w as x ∉ Φ_j(Z_j)). Let T_x be any subspace with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T_x. Since also HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x (range A) (x ∉ set (c)) and θ(x) > 0 (x ∈ M), uniqueness (`HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`) gives T_x = range A. For v ∈ T_x write v = As with s := A⁺v. Since U is open and f is locally Lipschitz on U, f is K-Lipschitz on some ball B_ρ(x) ⊆ U; by (DD), t ↦ f(x + tv) has derivative Bs at t = 0, and L(x)v = B A⁺ A s = Bs. Thus HasDerivAt (fun t => f (x + t • v)) (L x v) 0 for all v ∈ T_x. As Hⁿ(M ∖ G) = 0, this holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x.

6. (Local bound.) Let K ⊆ U be compact. For each z ∈ K choose ρ_z > 0 and K_z with B_{2ρ_z}(z) ⊆ U and f K_z-Lipschitz on B_{2ρ_z}(z) (U open, f locally Lipschitz on U). Finitely many balls B_{ρ_{z_l}}(z_l) cover K; let C := max_l K_{z_l} and ρ := min_l ρ_{z_l}. For x ∈ K, B_ρ(x) ⊆ B_{2ρ_l}(z_l) for an l with x ∈ B_{ρ_l}(z_l), so f is C-Lipschitz on B_ρ(x). Now let x ∈ M ∩ K. If x ∉ ⋃_j P_j, L(x) = 0. Local bound: (DD) with a uniform Lipschitz constant on a finite ball cover of K gives ‖L(x)‖ ≤ C on M ∩ K.

Then S is integer multiplicity.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is Steps 4–8 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, printed 3.4–3.9), with the cited results of Simon Ch. 2–3 supplied by the siblings. Setting: U ⊆ ℝ^P, V ⊆ ℝ^Q open; IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ with θ(x) ∈ ℕ for x ∈ M (so θ ≥ 1 on M by `pos`); T = τ(M,θ,ξ); f locally Lipschitz on U with f(U) ⊆ V; f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt T compact for every compact K ⊆ V; L : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P,ℝ^Q) Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable with the derivative clause (for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x, every weighted approximate tangent space T_x of (M,θ) at x and every v ∈ T_x, t ↦ f(x + tv) has derivative L(x)v at 0); S ∈ Dₙ(V) with S(ω) = ∫_M θ (L_#ξ)(ω∘f) dHⁿ for all ω ∈ Dⁿ(V). Notation: J(x) := ‖L(x)_#ξ(x)‖, M₊ := {x ∈ M : J(x) > 0}, ⟨β, ζ⟩ := ζ(β) for a covector β and an n-vector ζ. For x ∈ M write T_x for the weighted approximate tangent space when it exists (unique as θ(x) > 0, `HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`).

0. (Degenerate dimensions.) If n > P then Hⁿ ≡ 0 on ℝ^P, so S = 0; if n > Q then every n-covector on ℝ^Q is 0, hence every n-vector on ℝ^Q is 0 and S = 0. In both cases S = τ(∅, 1, 0): IsRectifiableTriple V n ∅ 1 0 holds trivially (∅ ⊆ V, measurable, Hⁿ(∅) = 0 so countably rectifiable, `pos` vacuous, integrable on ∅, every a.e. statement for the zero measure Hⁿ⌞∅ holds), the integer clause is vacuous, and tauAction over ∅ is 0. From now on n ≤ min(P, Q). For n = 0 all steps below hold verbatim (ℝ⁰ is a point, simple 0-vectors are ±simpleNVector ∅ of norm 1).

1. (Measurability, σ-finiteness, a.e. structure.) x ↦ L(x)_#ξ(x) and J are a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M ((A,w) ↦ A_#w is continuous), so M₊ is Hⁿ-null-measurable. Since θ ≥ 1 and θ is integrable on M ∩ K for compact K ⊆ U, Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞; U is σ-compact, so Hⁿ⌞M (and Hⁿ⌞A for A ⊆ M) is σ-finite. By `orients` and the clause, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M: T_x exists, T_x = span τ(x) for an orthonormal τ(x) with ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector τ(x), and L(x)τ_i(x) = d/dt f(x + tτ_i(x))|_{t=0}; call such x regular.

2. (Local Jacobian bound.) For compact K ⊆ U there is Λ_K with J(x) ≤ Λ_Kⁿ for every regular x ∈ M ∩ K: cover K by finitely many balls B_{ρ_l}(z_l) with f Λ_K-Lipschitz on B_{2ρ_l}(z_l) ⊆ U (U open, f locally Lipschitz); for regular x ∈ K the difference quotients of t ↦ f(x + tτ_i) are bounded by Λ_K, so |L(x)τ_i| ≤ Λ_K, and L(x)_#ξ(x) = ±simpleNVector(L(x)τ) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`), whence J(x) ≤ Π_i |L(x)τ_i| ≤ Λ_Kⁿ.

3. (Induced orientation; printed 3.4–3.5.) Let x ∈ M₊ be regular and v := L(x)τ(x). By simple_nvector_algebra (first conjunct), J(x)² = det G(v) > 0, so v is linearly independent and P_x := span v = L(x)(T_x) is an n-plane. Gram–Schmidt gives an orthonormal basis σ of P_x with v = Bσ, B invertible; by simple_nvector_algebra, simpleNVector v = det(B) • simpleNVector σ and ‖simpleNVector σ‖ = 1, so J(x) = |det B| and η_x := L(x)_#ξ(x)/J(x) = ±simpleNVector σ. Thus η_x is a unit simple n-vector orienting P_x, and L(x)_#ξ(x) = J(x)η_x. On M ∖ M₊, L_#ξ = 0. Hence S(ω) = ∫_{M₊} θ J ⟨ω∘f, η⟩ dHⁿ.

4. (Consequences of the area formula; printed 3.6.) We use the sibling lemma rectifiable_area_formula: for null-measurable A ⊆ M and a.e.-measurable h ≥ 0, the fibre-sum function N_A^h(y) := Σ_{x∈A∩f⁻¹(y)} h(x) is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable on ℝ^Q and ∫_A hJ dHⁿ = ∫_{ℝ^Q} N_A^h dHⁿ. We also use that for null-measurable A ⊆ M the image f(A) is Hⁿ-null-measurable (locally_lipschitz_image (ii); Hⁿ⌞A is σ-finite by step 1), so ∫ 1_{f(A)} dHⁿ = Hⁿ(f(A)).
 (a) If E ⊆ ℝ^Q is Hⁿ-null then Hⁿ(M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(E)) = 0: take a Borel Hⁿ-null E′ ⊇ E; A := M₊ ∩ f⁻¹(E′) is null-measurable (f is continuous on U ⊇ M); with h = 1, ∫_A J = ∫ #(A ∩ f⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = 0 since the integrand vanishes off E′; as J > 0 on A, Hⁿ(A) = 0.
 (b) For compact K ⊆ V let K′ := f⁻¹(K) ∩ spt T (compact, ⊆ U). With A := M₊ ∩ K′ and h := θ: ∫_K Σ_{x∈M₊∩K′∩f⁻¹(y)} θ(x) dHⁿ(y) ≤ ∫_{M₊∩K′} θ J dHⁿ ≤ Λ_{K′}ⁿ ∫_{M∩K′} θ dHⁿ < ∞ (step 2); with h := 1 and θ ≥ 1, since f(M₊ ∩ K′) is null-measurable and the counting function is ≥ 1 on it, Hⁿ(f(M₊ ∩ K′)) ≤ ∫ #(M₊∩K′∩f⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{M₊∩K′} J ≤ ∫_{M₊∩K′} θJ < ∞.
 (c) Hⁿ(f(M ∖ M₊)) = 0: with A := M ∖ M₊, h := 1, ∫ #((M∖M₊) ∩ f⁻¹(y)) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{M∖M₊} J = 0, and the integrand is ≥ 1 on the null-measurable set f(M ∖ M₊). Also Hⁿ(f(M ∖ spt T)) = 0 by the siblings rectifiable_support_null and locally_lipschitz_image (part (i)).

5. (The image Y.) Y := f(M₊) ⊆ f(U) ⊆ V. Y is Hⁿ-null-measurable by locally_lipschitz_image (part (ii); M₊ ⊆ U null-measurable with Hⁿ⌞M₊ σ-finite, step 1). For compact K ⊆ V, Y ∩ K ⊆ f(M₊ ∩ K′) ∪ f(M ∖ spt T), so Hⁿ(Y ∩ K) < ∞ by 4(b),(c).

6. (Source pieces on which f is an injective C¹ immersion; printed “f|M ∩ B_δ(x) is a diffeomorphism onto an embedded C¹ manifold”.) By countably_rectifiable_c1_cover take charts (Φ_j, Ω_j) of M (C¹, Lipschitz and antilipschitz on Ω_j), with Ω_j replaced by the open set Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(U); Ψ_j := (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹ is Lipschitz; M_j := (M ∩ Φ_j(Ω_j)) ∖ ⋃_{i<j} Φ_i(Ω_i) are disjoint with Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j M_j) = 0; u_j := f∘Φ_j is locally Lipschitz on Ω_j. Fix j. By chart_chain_rule, for Lⁿ-a.e. w ∈ Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(M), with x := Φ_j(w): T_x = range DΦ_j(w) and Du_j(w) = L(x)∘DΦ_j(w); moreover (Ψ_j maps Hⁿ-null sets to Lⁿ-null sets) x is regular for a.e. such w. At such w with x ∈ M₊: L(x) is injective on T_x (step 3: the L(x)τ_i are independent) and DΦ_j(w) : ℝⁿ → T_x is bijective, so Du_j(w) is injective. Apply lipschitz_c1_immersion_pieces to u_j on Ω_j: C¹ maps G_{j,k}, open O_{j,k} with G_{j,k} antilipschitz on O_{j,k}, disjoint Borel E_{j,k} ⊆ O_{j,k} ∩ Ω_j with u_j = G_{j,k} and Du_j = DG_{j,k} on E_{j,k}, covering a.e. point of injectivity of Du_j. Let W_j ⊆ Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(M₊ ∩ M_j) be the (null-measurable) set of w satisfying all the above and lying in ⋃_k E_{j,k}; Lⁿ((Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(M₊ ∩ M_j)) ∖ W_j) = 0. Put A_{j,k} := Φ_j(W_j ∩ E_{j,k}). Then:
 (i) the A_{j,k} are pairwise disjoint subsets of M₊ (M_j disjoint in j, E_{j,k} disjoint in k, Φ_j injective) and Hⁿ-null-measurable (locally_lipschitz_image (ii) applied to Φ_j);
 (ii) Hⁿ(M₊ ∖ ⋃_{j,k} A_{j,k}) = 0: M₊ ∩ M_j ∖ ⋃_k A_{j,k} is the Φ_j-image of an Lⁿ-null set (Φ_j Lipschitz), and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j M_j) = 0;
 (iii) for x = Φ_j(w) ∈ A_{j,k}: f(x) = u_j(w) = G_{j,k}(w) and, by uniqueness of Fréchet derivatives, L(x)∘DΦ_j(w) = Du_j(w) = DG_{j,k}(w); hence P_x = L(x)(T_x) = range DG_{j,k}(w);

 Re-index the pairs (j,k) by k ∈ ℕ: pieces A_k, charts (G_k, O_k), inverses Γ_k, and Y_k := f(A_k) ⊆ Y ∩ G_k(O_k) (null-measurable by locally_lipschitz_image (ii)). For x ∈ A_k let w_x := Γ_k(f(x)) be its parameter; then P_x = range DG_k(w_x).

Let Z_k := A_k ∩ f⁻¹(E_{2,k}) (Hⁿ-null by 4(a)), B := (M₊ ∖ ⋃_k A_k) ∪ ⋃_k Z_k ∪ {x ∈ M₊ : x not regular} (Hⁿ-null, ⊆ U) and E := ⋃_k E_{2,k} ∪ f(B) (Hⁿ-null by locally_lipschitz_image (i)). For y ∈ Y ∖ E put F_y := f⁻¹(y) ∩ M₊. Then F_y ⊆ spt T, so F_y ⊆ K_i′ whenever y ∈ K_i, hence Σ_{x∈F_y} θ(x) < ∞; since θ ≥ 1, F_y is finite, and F_y ≠ ∅. By steps 3 and 7 each η_x (x ∈ F_y) is ±simpleNVector σ for an orthonormal basis σ of Π_y.
